id: random-relators-kill-small-simple-quotients-of-kazhdan-groups
kind: claim
title: Boundedly many random relators of length L in a Kazhdan group kill every alternating quotient of order at most lambda^(-L)
distinct_from:
  sp21-lattice-few-alternating-and-large-rank-quotients: that asks for finitely many alternating quotients of one lattice in total; this kills, with high probability, the alternating quotients below an exponential threshold in any Kazhdan group and says nothing above it
---

**ESTABLISHED.** Let `Γ` have property (T) and be generated by `d` elements.
Let `S` be a finite symmetric generating set with Kazhdan constant `κ > 0`, and
put `λ = 1 - κ^2/(4|S|)`. Let `w_1,...,w_k` be independent lazy random walks of
length `L` on `Γ`, with step law `(δ_1 + uniform(S))/2`.

1. **Mixing bound.** For every finite quotient `χ: Γ ->> F` and every `x ∈ F`,
   `Pr[χ(w_i) = x] <= 1/|F| + λ^L`.
2. **Union bound.** Let `𝓕` be any set of isomorphism types of finite groups.
   The expected number of normal subgroups `N ⊴ Γ` such that
   - `Γ/N ∈ 𝓕`,
   - `|Γ/N| <= λ^(-L)`, and
   - `w_1,...,w_k ∈ N`

   is at most `Σ_(F ∈ 𝓕) |F|^d (2/|F|)^k`.
3. **Alternating quotients.** For `𝓕 = {Alt(m) : m >= 5}` the bound is at most
   `2^(d+1) 30^(-(k-d))`. So when `k >= d + log_30(2^(d+1)/ε)`, with probability
   at least `1 - ε` the group `Γ/<<w_1,...,w_k>>` has no quotient `Alt(m)` with
   `m!/2 <= λ^(-L)`. That is roughly every degree `m <= c L / log L`, with `c`
   depending on `κ` and `|S|`.

**Remark (all simple quotients).** CFSG gives that at most two finite simple
groups share an order; that statement was not re-read in this pass. Granting
it, part 2 extends the same threshold to every nonabelian finite simple
quotient. The abelian simple quotients are finitely many, because `Γ^ab` is
finite.

## What it says about fillings of an Sp(2,1) lattice

- **Small quotients die.** Random quotients do kill small alternating
  quotients: every one of order at most `λ^(-L)` dies with high probability.
- **Large quotients are untouched.** For fixed `L` the sum
  `Σ |F|^d (1/|F| + λ^L)^k` diverges over the large quotients, so no counting
  argument at one relator length reaches them. Above the threshold, a quotient
  `Γ/N` survives exactly when every relator lies in `N`.
- **What survives is a separation failure.** The obstruction left after a random
  quotient is a family of large alternating or large-rank quotients whose kernels
  all contain the same nontrivial elements. That is a failure of
  `sp21-noncongruence-simple-kernels-separate-points` at the relators.
- **No hyperbolicity claim.** Nothing here asserts that the random quotient is
  hyperbolic.

Proof in `random-relators-kill-small-simple-quotients-proof`. This is a
standard expander-mixing and union-bound argument; no novelty is claimed.
Not Lean-verified.
